newsitem.title: UK: NWE physical gas oil up with futures, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: NWE physical gas oil up with futures, trade thin.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices gained ground in line with firmer futures but trade was thin early on Wednesday.
Sellers premiums for spot barges were steady at August IPE +1.50 a tonne, but with buyers sidelined some brokers felt premiums would need to come off and no early deals were reported.
The firm dollar left few German end-users willing to buy and the inland German refiners took out any buying interest.
"The inland (German) majors are selling and are pushing hard. Importers have no chance," one broker said.
"There's just no buying around. I guess levels will have to come down," one trader said.

Brokers said the bottleneck at the jointly owned BP, Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam was set to continue and the refinery owners were asking those due to lift as late as the 18th to come a day late.

Diesel cargo premiums for prompt delivery into France were hovering around August IPE +$4.50 a tonne. Early August barrels were slightly firmer at +$5.00 while second half of the month barrels were pegged around August IPE +$4.75 a tonne.
Russian gas oil premiums were falling as prompt supplies increased and some saw the market as low as parity with the IPE screen.
"It depends on the volume. If you have a 10,000 tonnes for Bremen you could get a premium of (Aug IPE) +$2.50-$3.00 but a 60Kt Russian would only get (IPE) screen flat," one cargo trader said.
